grade: Illustrative multiplier scenario, not a field i-Tree Eco run, planting-capacity estimate or dispersion model.

program.species_tall_segments: green walls + honeylocust (Gleditsia triacanthos inermis), open crown, no canopy closure
program.species_shallow_segments: honeylocust, Kentucky coffeetree, zelkova; no London plane or dense-crown species in H/W>0.5 segments
program.salt_tolerance: honeylocust, coffeetree, zelkova rated salt-tolerant (Cornell Urban Horticulture Institute)

deegan_cap.note: Archived unsurveyed 12.9-acre scenario. The 25 lb/year illustration does not apply to the 2.02-acre model. A lid moves exhaust to portals and does not remove the source.

honesty: A modeled mass-removal total of 10.6 lb/year cannot predict concentration change in µg/m³. The maximum +1.29 µg/m³ monitor is unlocated in the public abstract. The earlier 8–15% concentration-reduction claim is withdrawn.

validation_notes.pm25_rate_source: Historical NYC value 0.24 g/m²/year, Nowak et al. (2013); USDA reproduction Table 1.
validation_notes.capacity: 180 trees is an assumed program, not calculated capacity in six bays.
validation_notes.maturity: 7 m crown diameter per tree assumes maturity; not a planting-day benefit.
validation_notes.other_pollutants: NO2 is a US-average proxy. O3 rate is untraced. Neither supports a claim of underestimation.
validation_notes.stormwater: 7.2 million US gallons/year is an unvalidated complete-program illustration.
